candidates.title: Operando cobalt-state comparison under TEOA versus TEA
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA in the primary P01 Co-bpy/g-C3N4 CO2-photoreduction formulation changes observable cobalt oxidation-state, coordination, or stability signatures during operation, and whether any donor-dependent state difference tracks catalytic output.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the P01 TEOA-based CoCl2+bpy+g-C3N4 formulation and motivates TEA as a comparator within the same family. EV052, EV076, EV088, GX008, and EV068 support operando or near-operando XAS plus complementary UV-vis/Raman/IR style characterization as a way to monitor catalyst state during CO2 reduction rather than relying only on recovered samples. GX001, GX005, and GX011 justify testing whether donor identity could alter cobalt coordination/speciation, but these are transferred from other cobalt or bipyridine-related systems and do not establish the same chemistry here. EV085 cautions that donor decomposition or decomposition-derived catalysts can confound interpretation, so signals must be treated as descriptive unless assignments are independently validated.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-variable test of whether donor identity changes cobalt-state observables or stability trends under matched turnover conditions; any correlated product shift is associative, not alone proof of causation.

Tests whether the TEOA formulation shows illumination-dependent cobalt-state changes beyond dark-state coordination or storage effects; this is not a pure causal test because timepoint handling also differs.
Tests whether the TEA formulation shows illumination-dependent cobalt-state changes beyond dark-state donor interaction or preparation effects; again a multi-factor descriptive contrast.
Bounds spectral and product backgrounds from donor, support, ligand, and cell components so cobalt-linked features are not assigned from matrix signals alone.

procedure: Prepare a single verified P01 baseline formulation, then generate TEOA and TEA variants by donor substitution only; confirm matched reactor geometry, gas handling, optical path, and analytical workflow before operando measurements.

Collect pre-illumination reference spectra for each group, then acquire operando or near-operando Co-focused XAS and complementary UV-vis during CO2 photoreaction; include synchronized product sampling for CO and H2 on the same runs if signal levels permit.
Run dark references with matched hold times and a no-cobalt illuminated reference to identify donor/support backgrounds and non-photochemical changes.

Analyze donor-dependent spectral evolution using internal consistency checks such as edge/feature shifts, coordination-shell fitting where justified, and time alignment with catalytic output; avoid unique species claims unless independent observables agree.
measurements: Co K-edge XANES features versus time, including edge position and pre-edge/white-line changes where detectable
EXAFS-derived coordination-shell changes versus time, reported as model-dependent if multiple fits remain plausible
Complementary UV-vis spectral evolution of the reaction mixture or suspended system under matched sampling state
CO and H2 product amounts or rates from the same reaction runs to test correlation with spectral evolution
Dark and no-cobalt background spectra to identify non-cobalt or non-photochemical contributions
If added, note that recovered-sample spectra are post-reaction references only and cannot establish the true operating state
candidates.supports: Support for H04 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference between E19G01 and E19G02 in operando or near-operando cobalt-linked observables under otherwise matched conditions, especially if the TEA and TEOA runs show different spectral evolution trajectories, coordination trends, or decay patterns that align with different CO/H2 outputs, while no-cobalt backgrounds do not explain the signal. Additional support would come from one donor showing stronger illumination-dependent change relative to its dark reference, consistent with different cobalt-manifold formation or deactivation.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H04 would be that E19G01 and E19G02 show indistinguishable cobalt-linked spectral features and temporal evolution within method resolution, similar dark-versus-light behavior, and similar stability trends despite reproducible catalytic CO/H2 differences established elsewhere under the same matched conditions. That would weaken cobalt-speciation/deactivation as the main explanation and shift priority toward donor photochemistry or medium effects.
candidates.inconclusive: The result is inconclusive if cobalt signals are too weak, the suspension prevents reliable fitting, donor substitution changes optical or scattering backgrounds enough to obscure cobalt features, multiple cobalt species fit equally well, or product differences are not reproduced under the exact spectroscopic cell conditions. A donor-dependent spectral change without correlated product behavior is descriptive but not sufficient to assign catalytic relevance.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent numerical loadings or beam conditions. Use the literature-anchored P01 composition only after source verification. Pilot first to choose the lowest cobalt concentration and path length that still gives reproducible cobalt-edge signal above matrix background while preserving measurable CO/H2 formation in the spectroscopic cell. Match donor formulations by the same verified baseline recipe except donor identity. Calibrate illumination by equal reactor geometry and measured incident photon flux at the sample, then verify that both donor systems remain within a product-detection window during the spectroscopy run. If operando XAS is impractical, downgrade to near-operando rapid-transfer sampling with the same group structure and explicitly narrow claims.
candidates.limitations: Assignments may remain ambiguous because the active cobalt species in P01 is unresolved and support-associated, solution-phase, and decomposition-derived species may coexist. Operando XAS gives element-specific state information but cannot by itself prove the catalytic intermediate or exclude upstream donor photochemistry as the primary cause of selectivity. UV-vis changes are non-unique and may reflect donor, ligand, support, or scattering effects. Dark-versus-light contrasts here also differ in sampling mode or elapsed state, so they are descriptive controls rather than strict single-factor causal tests. No-cobalt background is included only for the TEOA matrix, so donor-specific non-cobalt background differences may still need follow-up if TEA introduces unique interference.

candidates.title: TEA versus TEOA pre-irradiation association with Co-bpy formulations
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes detectable pre-turnover association or coordination signatures of the Co-bpy formulation, which could predispose different catalytic states before photochemistry begins.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the target CoCl2+bpy, g-C3N4, MeCN/H2O, TEOA formulation family. GX005 shows spectrophotometric titration can detect axial coordination in a cobalt system, GX001 and EV048 motivate donor/coordination competition and 1H NMR titration as a transferable comparison tool. The proposal transfers these methods cautiously to ask only whether TEA and TEOA produce different pre-irradiation observables, not whether any observed adduct is the active catalytic species.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-variable test in the supported P01 precursor formulation: donor-dependent differences in spectral shifts, line shape changes, or saturation behavior would support nonequivalent preassociation before irradiation.
Tests whether TEA produces detectable interaction relative to donor-free precursor background; absence of change limits evidence for strong TEA preassociation under these conditions.
Tests whether TEOA produces detectable interaction relative to donor-free precursor background; stronger or distinct change than TEA would support additive-specific preassembly.

Cleaner analogue comparison checks whether any TEA/TEOA difference persists without g-C3N4; agreement with P01 would support transfer to cobalt-solution association, while disagreement would implicate support-associated complexity.

procedure: Prepare matched donor-free CoCl2+bpy precursor samples in the P01 solvent system, with and without g-C3N4 as defined by the selected platform variant, and record baseline spectra before amine addition.
Add TEA or TEOA in identical serial increments to separate matched samples while holding cobalt source, bpy, solvent composition, temperature, and non-irradiated handling constant.

After each increment, collect UV-Vis spectra and collect 1H NMR-style spectra only for sample states that remain sufficiently homogeneous and interpretable; retain donor-free references acquired over the same time window.

Use the simplest binding or association model justified by the data only if reproducible concentration-dependent changes exceed baseline drift; otherwise report descriptive differences and carry forward only bounded conclusions.
measurements: UV-Vis absorption changes of the precursor mixture as a function of TEA or TEOA addition, including wavelength shifts, new bands, intensity changes, and saturation behavior.
1H NMR chemical-shift or line-broadening changes for ligand and donor resonances in the simplified homogeneous analogue, with donor-free and amine-only references.
Replicate-to-replicate baseline drift and time-dependent changes in donor-free samples to distinguish true titration responses from precursor instability.

Qualitative sample-state observations such as precipitation or turbidity, because these can signal formulation changes but cannot by themselves establish coordination geometry or active-species identity.
candidates.supports: Support for H04 would be reproducible donor-dependent pre-irradiation observables under otherwise matched conditions, especially if TEA and TEOA give different shift patterns, different apparent association onset or saturation behavior, or one donor perturbs the Co-bpy precursor while the other does not. Concordant TEA-versus-TEOA differences in both the P01 precursor mixture and the simpler homogeneous analogue would strengthen transfer to cobalt-centered preassociation rather than a support-only artifact.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if TEA and TEOA give indistinguishable spectra within experimental resolution across matched titrations, while donor-free controls remain stable and the analogue also shows no donor-specific difference. That outcome would argue against strong pre-turnover donor-specific cobalt association as the main source of the CO/H2 difference, though it would not exclude differences arising later under irradiation.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if spectra are dominated by scattering from g-C3N4, if cobalt/bpy precursor instability masks titration responses, if only one method is interpretable, or if both donors alter bulk medium properties without a cobalt-specific signature. Any observed shift also remains non-diagnostic for the catalytically active state because pre-irradiation association need not persist during turnover.
candidates.parameter_selection: Use the literature-defined P01 composition family without inventing missing numerical values. First run a pilot with donor-free precursor to identify a time window over which baseline drift is acceptably small. Choose amine addition increments that span from no visible spectral change to either a reproducible plateau or the onset of non-ideal behavior such as precipitation; use the same increment scheme for TEA and TEOA. Attempt 1H NMR only on simplified homogeneous analogue samples that remain sufficiently resolved; if the P01 slurry is not NMR-interpretable, restrict NMR to the analogue and keep UV-Vis as the common measurement. If apparent binding-model fitting is unstable or non-unique, report descriptive titration trends instead of forcing equilibrium constants.
candidates.limitations: Most evidence is transferred from other cobalt families or other metals, so any assignment to direct cobalt coordination is provisional. P01 contains g-C3N4, so scattering and heterogeneous interfaces may obscure weak spectral changes. TEA and TEOA also change medium properties, so a spectral difference does not uniquely prove inner-sphere coordination. Conversely, no detectable change does not rule out transient or photoinduced interactions below detection limits. This characterization cannot establish product origin, catalytic necessity, or the identity of the true operating species under illumination.

candidates.title: Deactivation and catalyst persistence map
candidates.purpose: Test whether replacing TEOA with TEA changes time-dependent cobalt persistence, donor-dependent state drift, or loss of catalytic output in the primary Co-bpy/g-C3N4 platform, rather than only changing endpoint selectivity.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV059 anchors the primary CoCl2+bpy/g-C3N4/MeCN-H2O/TEOA platform and motivates a single-variable TEA comparator. EV051 and EV085 justify treating donor identity as a possible driver of catalyst stability, decomposition, or donor-derived confounding rather than assuming unchanged active species. EV004 and GX008 support paired operando or near-operando state tracking with catalytic time-course and rigorous controls. Proposed transfer: apply matched donor substitution within P01 and compare decay profiles and cobalt-state observables over time; this is a proposal, not a reported literature result for this exact system.

comparisons.inference: Primary test: if donor substitution changes catalytic decay profile and paired cobalt-state or persistence observables under otherwise matched conditions, that supports donor-linked cobalt speciation or deactivation contributions to the CO/H2 difference.
Necessity/background control for the TEOA condition: establishes whether time-dependent gas products or spectral changes require cobalt rather than arising from g-C3N4 plus donor alone.
Necessity/background control for the TEA condition: checks whether donor-dependent decay or product trends persist without cobalt, which would weaken a cobalt-state explanation.
Background donor comparison without cobalt: any donor-dependent background products or state-like signals here confound attribution of E21G01 versus E21G02 solely to cobalt chemistry.

procedure: Assemble matched P01 reaction mixtures for all groups using the literature-anchored component set; verify source-defined baseline composition where available and hold reactor geometry, gas handling, illumination program, and analytical workflow constant across groups.

Run photocatalysis under CO2 with repeated aliquot or headspace sampling at predefined time points; in parallel collect paired pre-reaction, during-reaction when feasible, and post-reaction cobalt-state measurements from matched samples for each donor condition.

Quantify CO and H2 at every time point and document whether signal grows, plateaus, or decays; for characterization collect cobalt-centered observables and note whether any assignment is direct, tentative, or unresolved.
Compare donor conditions by time-dependent output and state trajectories, then benchmark each against its no-cobalt control to exclude donor/support background behavior.

If operando acquisition is not feasible, use tightly timed near-operando freeze or rapid-transfer sampling validated by a pilot for minimal handling drift, and report conclusions as bounded by that limitation.
measurements: Time-resolved CO and H2 amounts from the same analytical method across all groups; these establish output and decay trends but not product origin by themselves.

Cobalt-centered state observables before, during, and after reaction using a transferable method such as XAS or another cobalt-sensitive spectroscopy; these can show donor-dependent valence or coordination changes but may not uniquely identify the active species.
Optional complementary UV-Vis, Raman, or IR signatures on matched samples to detect gross donor-dependent catalyst drift or new species; these are supportive only if assignments are validated.
Mass balance and visible precipitation or phase-change notes to flag catalyst loss or aggregation; these indicate persistence issues but cannot establish molecular identity.
No-cobalt control products and spectra to bound donor/support background contributions and prevent overassignment of donor-derived or support-derived signals to cobalt turnover.
candidates.supports: Support for H04 would be a reproducible donor-dependent difference between E21G01 and E21G02 in catalytic decay profile, cobalt persistence, or cobalt-state trajectory that is absent or much smaller in the no-cobalt controls. Stronger support is obtained if the donor giving different CO/H2 behavior also shows distinct cobalt-state drift or faster loss of cobalt-associated signal over time under otherwise matched conditions.
candidates.refutes: H04 is weakened if E21G01 and E21G02 show similar time-dependent CO and H2 evolution, similar catalyst persistence, and no reproducible donor-dependent difference in cobalt-state observables beyond measurement uncertainty, while no-cobalt controls remain low and uninformative. It is further weakened if donor-dependent catalytic differences occur without any detectable difference in cobalt-state or persistence despite adequate sensitivity.
candidates.inconclusive: Results are inconclusive if donor substitution changes multiple uncontrolled medium properties, if characterization sensitivity is insufficient to resolve cobalt under operating conditions, if no-cobalt controls show substantial donor-dependent background products or overlapping signals, or if only ex situ post-reaction differences are observed without validated linkage to the operating state.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent numeric settings. Use the source-anchored P01 formulation as the starting point and verify any missing concentrations, irradiation range, and sampling interval from the supplied source record before execution. Pilot rules: first confirm product signals are above blank and within the linear range of the product assay; choose time points dense enough to detect an early induction period, plateau, or decay; choose spectroscopic acquisition settings on concentrated matched samples or extended integration only after confirming that the method resolves cobalt above donor/support background; if operando signal is too weak, switch to a validated rapid-transfer near-operando workflow rather than claiming operating-state identity.
candidates.limitations: Direct literature evidence for a strict TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in this exact P01 recipe is incomplete. The active cobalt species is unresolved, so state changes may remain descriptive rather than structurally unique. TEA and TEOA can alter donor strength, proton handling, CO2 interaction, viscosity, and coordination simultaneously, so even the primary contrast does not isolate a single causal subfactor. No-cobalt controls bound some background chemistry but do not recreate the full catalytic manifold. Post-reaction characterization alone cannot establish the true operating state.
